metadata.description: SOILSTICE Backend Crop Knowledge Base covering all 14 canonical crops. Complete and 100% populated across CRP001 through CRP014 with verified scientific evidence.
metadata.notes: Applied controlled scientific remediations to Stage 4. Harmonized oilseed radish nitrogen accounting by setting net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha to null while preserving 0.0 kg N/ha BNF and 100-220 kg N/ha nitrate scavenging. Reclassified CRP013<->CRP014 from 'highly_compatible' to 'caution_conditional' to cleanly distinguish sequential monoculture rotation (atypical/unstudied) from simultaneous polyculture mixtures [MIXTURE NOTE]. Qualified brassica rotational risks as epidemiological disease management rather than statutory prohibitions. Qualified oilseed radish 2-3x infiltration, 5-10% corn yield bump, deep taproot penetration, winter-kill threshold, and biofumigation efficacy as site- and management-specific outcomes.

crop_identity.growth_habit: Erect summer annual C4 monocotyledonous graminoid

active_growth_duration_days.limitations: Reflects U.S. Corn Belt Comparative Relative Maturity (CRM 95-115 d rating); total calendar duration to harvest grain moisture (15-18%) typically spans 120-140 days.

calendar_occupancy_duration_days.limitations: Field occupancy from bare-soil planting to combine harvest.

growing_degree_days_base_temp_c.limitations: Modified 86/50 Method: base temperature cutoff is 10.0°C (50°F), upper cutoff is 30.0°C (86°F).

growing_degree_days_accumulated.limitations: Equates to 2,100 to 2,800 GDD-F from planting to physiological maturity (R6 black layer; Purdue AY-280-W).

vernalization_required.notes: Warm-season C4 grass; zero vernalization requirement for floral induction.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Modern temperate U.S. dent corn hybrids have been selected for functional day-neutrality.

growth_stages.description: Coleoptile penetrates soil surface; requires soil temp >=10°C.
Pollen shed and silk emergence; peak water and heat vulnerability.
Hard starch layer reaches kernel base; black layer forms; ~30-35% moisture.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Light frost (<0°C to -2°C) kills leaf tissue; growing point survives pre-V6 if soil does not freeze.

absolute_max_survival_c.limitations: Physiological thermal breakdown and irreversible photosynthetic enzyme denaturation.

frost_tolerance.description: Sensitive to sub-zero temperatures. Frost terminates canopy development in autumn; spring frost defoliates seedlings but growing point survives pre-V6.

heat_stress_threshold_c.limitations: Empirical county-level yield decline breakpoint under field conditions (Schlenker & Roberts 2009 PNAS); acute physiological pollen desiccation occurs at sustained temperatures >35.0°C.

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Severe silk desiccation, pollen sterility, and asynchronous anthesis-silking interval (ASI).

seasonal_effective_precipitation_max_mm.limitations: Upper bound of useful infiltration; not a waterlogging threshold.

soil_water_availability_context.description: Requires deep root profile with 150-200 mm available water capacity (AWC) to buffer short summer dry spells.

irrigation_requirement_context.description: Rainfed in Central/Eastern Corn Belt; supplemental or full irrigation (250-450 mm net) required in Western High Plains (KS, NE).

seasonal_consumptive_water_use_etc_mm.limitations: Total seasonal crop evapotranspiration (ETc); equates to 20-32 inches (22-30 inches in Great Plains via KSU C-560).

peak_daily_water_use_mm_day.limitations: Occurs during tassel, silking, and early blister stages.

drought_tolerance.description: High sensitivity during VT/R1 silking; 4 consecutive days of severe moisture stress reduces yield by up to 40-50%.

heat_tolerance.description: Tolerant vegetative growth under adequate moisture, but highly vulnerable during pollination (>35°C silk drying).

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Soil oxygen depletion occurs within ~48 hours. Stage dependent: pre-V6 corn dies in 24-48 h if water >24°C; post-V6 corn survives 3-5 days under cool (<18°C) water.

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Tolerates down to pH 5.5 without severe yield loss; at pH <5.0 aluminum toxicity restricts roots.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: Grown up to pH 7.8; higher pH induces zinc and iron chlorosis.

salinity_tolerance_ec_e_threshold_ds_m.limitations: Maas & Hoffman (1977) linear response model: saturated soil extract electrical conductivity threshold.

salinity_yield_decline_slope_percent.limitations: Percent yield loss per dS/m increase above 1.7 dS/m threshold: Yr = 100 - 12(ECe - 1.7).

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Moderately sensitive per USDA-ARS Maas-Hoffman classification.

soil_texture_preferences.notes: Deep prairie silt loams are premier Corn Belt soils.
High water-holding capacity and aeration.
Productive with tile drainage.
Requires frequent irrigation and split N applications.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: High seedling mortality from spring anoxia without drainage.

effective_water_extraction_depth_cm.limitations: Management-oriented effective root extraction zone (3.0 to 4.0 ft / 90 to 120 cm per USDA-NRCS NEH 652 Table 3-4 for mature field corn in deep, unrestricted soils). Subsoil compaction, fragipans, or high water tables restrict active rooting to 60-90 cm.

maximum_anatomical_root_depth_cm.limitations: Maximum anatomical vertical root elongation observed in deep, unconstrained loess profiles (Weaver 1926). Low root length density at depth (<0.1 cm/cm3); provides emergency buffer during drought but does not represent bulk uptake zone.

root_system_architecture.description: Seminal root system superseded by 5-6 whorls of nodal adventitious roots, capped by brace roots.

compaction_alleviation_potential.description: Fibrous root system is vulnerable to horizontal deflection by plow pans; poor bio-drilling capacity.

nitrogen_uptake_per_unit_yield.limitations: Equates to 1.1 to 1.2 lb N/bu total plant uptake; grain removal is ~0.75-0.80 lb N/bu.

phosphorus_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: 0.35 lb P2O5 per bushel grain removal (Tri-State Recommendations Bulletin 974).

potassium_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: 0.20 lb K2O per bushel grain removal (Tri-State Recommendations Bulletin 974). Stover contains additional 1.1 lb K2O/bu.

has_symbiotic_fixation_capacity.notes: Non-legume cereal; lacks symbiotic nitrogen-fixing nodule architecture.

net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha.limitations: Calculation boundary: Net soil mineral N depletion calculated as crop harvest N export (120-180 kg N/ha in grain) minus zero biological N fixation. Does not account for synthetic fertilizer additions or gaseous/leaching loss pathways.

nitrogen_balance_assessment.description: Major net extractive consumer of soil nitrogen; stover immobilizes soil N during early decomposition.

fertilizer_equivalent_n_credit_lb_ac.limitations: Corn provides zero net fertilizer N credit. High C:N stover (55:1 to 65:1) induces early spring microbial immobilization (~30-50 lb N/acre under high residue volumes; Gentry et al. 2013, EV0015), requiring 30-40 lb N/ac starter fertilizer in continuous corn.

credit_mechanism.description: Stover residue (high C:N ratio 55:1 to 65:1) immobilizes mineralized soil nitrogen during early spring microbial decomposition.

release_rate_timing.description: Decomposes over 18 to 24 months, gradually recycling potassium (~80-120 lb K2O/ac) and phosphorus back to soil.

aboveground_dry_matter_biomass_kg_ha.limitations: Equates to 3.5 to 5.0 dry tons/acre stover.

residue_decomposition_rate.description: Decomposes over 18-24 months; persistent residue protects soil from water and wind erosion.

ground_cover_rate.description: Provides >70-80% ground cover under no-till management; minimal cover if clean tilled.

erosion_reduction_potential.description: High erosion reduction when residue is retained on surface.

nitrate_scavenging_efficiency.description: Primary consumer of N; does not scavenge nitrate post-harvest.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Iowa MRTN rotational N savings (48-52 lb N/ac lower N requirement vs continuous corn; EV0014) and +10-15% corn yield boost (EV0015).
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Credit is an avoided stover immobilization / mineralization response, not additive nitrogen.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Extended 3-year rotation (Corn-Soybean-Wheat) boosts corn yields by 5-10% and breaks corn rootworm cycles.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Starter nitrogen (30-40 lb N/ac) banded at corn planting mitigates early-season wheat straw N tie-up.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Spring wheat stubble traps winter snow, conserving profile moisture for subsequent corn crop; August harvest allows fall tillage/fertilizer.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Requires starter fertilizer N at corn planting to overcome cold spring soil and residue N tie-up.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Breaks western and northern corn rootworm cycles; provides rotational break for corn foliar blights.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Sorghum residue immobilizes 20-30 lb N/ac; starter fertilizer N recommended at corn planting.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn is a non-host to reniform nematode (Rotylenchulus reniformis); rotating cotton with corn suppresses reniform populations and boosts subsequent cotton yields by 10-18% (MSU Pub 2426, EV0096).
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: If root-knot nematode is the predominant species, rotating cotton with corn does not provide a biological break.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn planted on beds following furrow-irrigated rice (FIR / row rice) or well-drained silt loam ground; breaks rice diseases and exploits deep profile fertility.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Compact subsoil hardpan from flooded rice can restrict corn root penetration unless subsoiled or planted on permanent raised beds.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Winter barley harvested early (late May to early June) allows planting double-crop silage corn or short-season grain corn in Mid-Atlantic/Upper South; spring barley stubble conserves snow in Northern Plains.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: In Mid-Atlantic and Upper South, winter barley harvest in early June enables double-crop silage or short-season grain corn. In Northern Great Plains, short thermal season precludes double-cropping; sequential corn is planted the following spring.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Breaks corn rootworm and foliar leaf blights; standard Corn Belt rotational sequence boosting soybean yields 5-10% over monoculture.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Standard atrazine plant-back interval to soybean is the following spring (do not plant soybean in same season).

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Provides winter ground cover and erosion defense following corn silage or early-harvest grain corn.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Requires resistant wheat varieties, triazole fungicide at anthesis, and compliance with atrazine plant-back intervals.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Feasible in southern fringes of spring wheat belt (SE North Dakota, W Minnesota) following early-maturing corn.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Heavy corn residue must be managed to allow uniform spring wheat emergence; fungicide application at flowering required.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn precedes sorghum well; allows utilizing high residual soil fertility in dryland rotations.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Ensure sorghum seed is safened (Concep III) if chloroacetamide herbicides are applied.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn residue shields emerging cotton seedlings from wind abrasion on sandy Coastal Plain soils.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Requires strict avoidance of atrazine in the corn phase, and intensive Bt monitoring or foliar insecticide management for migrating bollworm.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn breaks rice diseases; heavy corn stubble decomposed under winter flooding.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Strict atrazine prohibition: atrazine residues in anaerobic flooded soil cause severe seedling chlorosis and stand mortality in rice.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Feasible cereal rotation; corn residue protects soil from wind erosion.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Severe malting quality risk: avoid planting malting barley directly into corn stubble; require triazole fungicide at heading and scab-tolerant varieties.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Larvae hatch in spring and starve in non-host broadleaf root systems (except rotation-resistant variant).
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Behavioral western corn rootworm variant in IL/IN lays eggs in soybeans.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Crop rotation away from corn allows infected residue to decompose, reducing inoculum.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Windborne conidia can blow in from neighboring fields.

shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Avoid planting wheat directly into standing corn stalks without scab-tolerant wheat cultivars and triazole fungicides.
shared_pest_disease_risks.limitations: Causes Gibberella stalk/ear rot in corn and Head Scab in wheat.

weed_suppression_potential.description: Dense summer canopy suppresses late weeds; heavy stover residue suppresses early spring winter annuals.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: Rotate only to corn or sorghum until following year; if applied after June 10, rotate only to corn/sorghum the next year; in eastern Dakotas, KS, western MN, and NE, do not rotate to soybeans if rate exceeded 4 pt/A (2.0 lb a.i./A).
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: EPA master label text is legally binding.

continuous_monoculture_penalty.description: 5% to 15% yield loss in continuous corn compared to rotated corn across Corn Belt long-term trials (Gentry et al. 2013).

cover_crop_niche.description: Ideal candidate for post-harvest drilling of cereal rye (Secale cereale) or V4-V6 interseeding of crimson clover/radish.

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Spring cold wet soils delay planting; early autumn freeze before physiological maturity.
Requires short-season hybrids (CRM 80-95); early frost risk.
Severe summer heat and high VPD at pollination; heavy reliance on Ogallala Aquifer irrigation.

crop_identity.growth_habit: Bushy erect branched indeterminate or determinate summer annual C3 legume

active_growth_duration_days.limitations: Varies by Maturity Group (MG 000 in Northern Plains to MG VIII in Deep South).

growing_degree_days_accumulated.limitations: Equates to 1,800 to 2,600 GDD-F (Licht et al. 2014, ISU PMR 1004). Strongly modulated by photoperiod.

vernalization_required.notes: Photoperiod-sensitive short-day plant; zero vernalization requirement.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Classic short-day photoperiodic floral induction. Flowering triggered as night length exceeds critical dark threshold, defining commercial Maturity Groups.

growth_stages.description: Hypocotyl arch pulls cotyledons through soil; sensitive to crusting.

growth_stages.stage_name: Beginning Pod to Full Seed (R3 to R6)
growth_stages.description: Pod enlargement and seed filling; peak moisture and nutrient extraction.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Vegetative foliage damaged at <0°C; severe frost kill below -1.5°C.

frost_tolerance.description: Highly sensitive to frost at all stages; emergence hook (VE) and flowers killed by < -1°C.

heat_stress_threshold_c.limitations: Empirical county-level yield decline breakpoint (Schlenker & Roberts 2009 PNAS); floral abortion increases above 35.0°C (Gibson & Mullen 1996).

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Floral abortion and pod drop, partially buffered by indeterminate flowering habit.

soil_water_availability_context.description: Requires soil moisture buffering during August pod-fill (R4-R5).

irrigation_requirement_context.description: Overwhelmingly rainfed in the Midwest; furrow or center-pivot irrigated in the Mississippi Delta and Western Plains.

seasonal_consumptive_water_use_etc_mm.limitations: Total seasonal crop evapotranspiration (ETc); equates to 18-26 inches (KSU C-449).

peak_daily_water_use_mm_day.limitations: Occurs during pod development and rapid seed fill.

drought_tolerance.description: Moderate tolerance during vegetative growth; highly vulnerable during R3-R5 where moisture stress causes pod abortion.

heat_tolerance.description: Tolerant vegetative growth; high heat (>35°C) at flowering increases pod abortion.

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Tolerates saturated soils for ~48 hours. Beyond 48 hours, root anoxia kills Bradyrhizobium nodules and Phytophthora root rot escalates.

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Rhizobia nodulation declines below pH 5.8; aluminum toxicity below 5.2.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: High pH (>7.4) calcareous soils trigger severe Iron Deficiency Chlorosis (IDC).

salinity_yield_decline_slope_percent.limitations: Yr = 100 - 20(ECe - 5.0). Moderately tolerant per Maas & Hoffman (1977).

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Moderately tolerant to soil salinity per Maas & Hoffman.

soil_texture_preferences.notes: Excellent seedbed and moisture retention.
Optimal root and nodule development.
Productive, but watch for crusting at emergence.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: Tolerates slightly heavier soils than corn.
Anoxic nodule death and Phytophthora rot.

effective_water_extraction_depth_cm.limitations: Primary soybean field lysimeter and core sampling trials (Mayaki et al. 1976; Weaver 1926). Active moisture extraction concentrated in upper 60 to 90 cm (up to 100 cm in deep silt loam). Note: USDA-NRCS NEH Table 3-4 does not explicitly index soybean; values derive from peer-reviewed field trials. Claypans restrict roots to 45-75 cm.

maximum_anatomical_root_depth_cm.limitations: Maximum vertical taproot penetration in deep loose soils (Weaver 1926; Mayaki et al. 1976). Secondary lateral branching concentrated in top 15-30 cm where Bradyrhizobium nodules reside.

root_system_architecture.description: Prominent vertical taproot system with dense secondary laterals in upper 15-30 cm where nodules concentrate.

compaction_alleviation_potential.description: Central taproot exerts greater vertical penetration pressure than fibrous cereal roots.

nitrogen_uptake_per_unit_yield.limitations: Equates to 3.3 to 4.0 lb N/bu total plant uptake (approx. 50-60% fixed biologically).

phosphorus_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: Tri-State Recommendations: 0.80 lb P2O5 per bushel of grain.

potassium_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: Tri-State Recommendations: 1.15 lb K2O per bushel of grain.

rhizobium_symbiont_species.description: Inoculation recommended in fields with no recent soybean history.

effective_fixation_conditions.description: High residual soil nitrate inhibits nodule formation; optimal fixation under low starter N.

net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha.limitations: Calculation boundary per Salvagiotti et al. (2008, Table 2; EV0041): Defined as gross biological N2 fixation minus harvested grain N export in aboveground biomass trials (-80 to +40 kg N/ha reported across literature; modal range -20 to +15 kg N/ha). When root biomass and rhizodeposition are estimated (+10 to +20 kg N/ha), net balance remains essentially neutral under high grain yield conditions. Does not include gaseous denitrification or nitrate leaching losses.

nitrogen_balance_assessment.description: 70-80% of fixed N is exported in seed, resulting in near-neutral net soil N change.

fertilizer_equivalent_n_credit_lb_ac.limitations: Calculation boundary: Evaluated specifically for Corn Following Soybean (CS) compared to Corn Following Corn (CC) under the Midwest Maximum Return to Nitrogen (MRTN) framework (Sawyer et al. 2006, Iowa State PM 1714 / PM 2015; EV0014). For Main Iowa Region at 0.10 price ratio ($0.50/lb N, $5.00/bu corn), MRTN rate for CS is 136-140 lb N/acre vs 185-188 lb N/acre for CC, yielding a ~48-52 lb N/acre differential (broadly generalized as 30-50 lb N/ac across Corn Belt). This differential is an empirical rotational response reflecting multiple interacting mechanisms: lower microbial immobilization compared to corn stover, rapid mineralization of low C:N residue (20:1-30:1), and altered soil biology—NOT an additive excretion of fixed N from soybean nodules into the soil profile.

credit_mechanism.description: Multi-factorial empirical rotation effect: lower microbial immobilization than corn stover, rapid mineralization of low C:N residue, and enhanced soil microbial diversity under crop rotation (Sawyer et al. 2006; Salvagiotti et al. 2008).

release_rate_timing.description: Residue breaks down within 30-60 days in spring, releasing mineralized N in synchronization with early corn uptake.

aboveground_dry_matter_biomass_kg_ha.limitations: Equates to 1.5 to 2.5 dry tons/acre residue.

residue_decomposition_rate.description: ~68% dry weight lost after 32 days in field litterbags (Broder & Wagner 1988); leaves soil mellow and prone to erosion.

ground_cover_rate.description: Low residue durability; leaves soil surface fragile post-harvest unless cover crop is planted.

erosion_reduction_potential.description: Leaves soil vulnerable in winter; highly benefits from cover cropping.

nitrate_scavenging_efficiency.description: N fixer; leaves mineral N post-harvest.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Breaks corn rootworm and foliar leaf blights; standard Corn Belt rotational sequence boosting soybean yields 5-10% over monoculture.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Standard atrazine plant-back interval to soybean is the following spring (do not plant soybean in same season).

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Double-crop soybean drilled immediately into harvested wheat stubble. Practiced primarily south of approximately 39°–40°N latitude as a conditional regional rule of thumb (UK Bulletin ID-185, EV0066). In favorable seasons with early wheat harvest (mid-June, 18-20% grain moisture with artificial drying) and adequate soil moisture, double-cropping successfully extends up to 41°–42°N (northern IN/OH, southern MI/WI) using early-maturing cultivars (Maturity Groups 1.5–2.5).
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Conditional regional rule of thumb, NOT an absolute physical cutoff. Primary constraints are thermal accumulation (frost-free days remaining before autumn freeze) and late-June/July topsoil moisture for soybean emergence. Delaying double-crop soybean planting past late June imposes a documented yield penalty of 0.5 to 1.0 bu/acre per day of delay (EV0066).

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Spring wheat harvest in August creates an early window for fall weed control and fertilizer application ahead of next spring's soybean.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Northern Plains thermal deficit precludes double-cropping; sequential full-season soybean is planted the following spring (EV0071).

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Sorghum is a non-host to Soybean Cyst Nematode (Heterodera glycines), suppressing nematode populations; heavy sorghum stubble reduces soil evaporation ahead of soybean.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Ensure atrazine rates on sorghum do not exceed labeled rates for subsequent soybean planting.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Alternating broadleaf taproot and fibrous root architecture; soybean fixes nitrogen, improving soil health for cotton.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: In fields infested with reniform nematode, rotating cotton with soybean maintains high nematode pressure without providing a sanitizing break.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Premier crop sequence in the Mid-South (1:1 or 2:1 Rice-Soybean); aerobic soybean phase breaks sheath blight fungal sclerotia, allows selective chemical control of weedy red rice with ACCase/ALS herbicides, and restores soil structure.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Heavy clay rice ground must be bedded or surface-drained to prevent soybean waterlogging during summer rains.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Winter barley matures 1 to 2 weeks earlier than winter wheat, enabling double-crop soybean planting by early to mid-June with 100% full-season yield potential in Mid-Atlantic and Upper South (VCE Pub 424-035, EV0126).
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Requires immediate no-till drilling of soybean into standing barley stubble following combine harvest to conserve seedbed moisture.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Iowa MRTN rotational N savings (48-52 lb N/ac lower N requirement vs continuous corn; EV0014) and +10-15% corn yield boost (EV0015).
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Credit is an avoided stover immobilization / mineralization response, not additive nitrogen.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean harvest in September/October creates an ideal, mellow seedbed for no-till drilling winter wheat; wheat provides winter ground cover.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Requires early-maturing soybean harvest (late Sep / early Oct) to ensure wheat emergence before winter dormancy (EV0066).

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean residue breaks cereal root rot cycles (take-all) and leaves soil mellow for early spring drill penetration in April/May (EV0071).
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Soybean leaves fragile low-residue cover, increasing spring wind erosion vulnerability prior to wheat canopy closure.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean provides an avoided-immobilization rotational benefit (30-45 lb N/ac equivalent savings) and boosts subsequent sorghum yield by 10-15% over monoculture.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Fomesafen carryover can cause severe sorghum seedling bleaching on low-OM, high-pH western soils.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean provides rotational nitrogen savings (20-30 lb N/ac equivalent) and leaves mellow soil for cotton bedding.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: High reniform nematode risk; verify herbicide carryover and auxin trait compatibility before planting cotton.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean residue mineralizes readily under flood; rice yields follow a 10-15% rotational boost over continuous rice; soybean breaks the red rice seedbank.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Ensure soybean fields are leveled and levee survey lines re-established prior to rice planting.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Early soybean harvest in September/October creates a mellow, low-residue seedbed for fall winter barley drilling; soybean breaks barley foliar blotch cycles.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Observe fomesafen plant-back intervals before drilling fall winter barley.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Larvae hatch and starve in broadleaf roots.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Behavioral western corn rootworm variant in IL/IN.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Soybean is a non-host; interrupts fungal mycelium survival in soil.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Effective when rotation interval is at least 1 full year.

shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Avoid planting susceptible broadleaf cover crops immediately preceding soybeans in fields with white mold history.
shared_pest_disease_risks.limitations: Sclerotia persist in soil for 5-7 years.

weed_suppression_potential.description: Rapid canopy closure in 15- or 30-inch rows suppresses in-season weeds; leaves minimal residue post-harvest.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: 10-month rotational plant-back interval to field corn. Region 4a Specific Restriction: Must not be applied later than June 20, and cumulative rainfall plus overhead irrigation must total at least 15 inches; if not met, plant only soybeans the following season.
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: EPA master label text is legally binding.

continuous_monoculture_penalty.description: 10% to 20% cumulative yield decline in continuous soybean due to exponential SCN egg density increases and soilborne disease escalation (CPN-5001, EV0026).

cover_crop_niche.description: Outstanding candidate for drilling cereal rye immediately following soybean harvest to protect fragile residue.

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Spring crusting, Sudden Death Syndrome in wet cold springs, early autumn frost.
Requires early maturity groups (MG 000-I); Iron Deficiency Chlorosis (IDC) on high-pH soils.
High humidity foliar diseases, nematodes, late-season drought.

crop_identity.growth_habit: Winter annual graminoid requiring vernalization cold exposure for floral induction

active_growth_duration_days.limitations: Active biological cell division days only; excludes 90 to 120 days of overwinter dormancy.

calendar_occupancy_duration_days.limitations: Total field occupancy from autumn drilling (Sep-Oct) to mid-summer harvest (Jun-Jul).

growing_degree_days_accumulated.limitations: Fall establishment ~400-600 GDD-C; spring green-up to maturity ~1,300-1,750 GDD-C.

vernalization_required.notes: Obligate vernalization cold requirement: 4 to 8 weeks (30 to 60 days) of cumulative temperatures between 0°C and 7°C required for vegetative-to-reproductive transition in standard winter wheat (Yan et al. 2003 PNAS, EV0045; Simmons & Oelke, EV0048).
vernalization_required.genotype_variation_notes: Cultivar dependent: facultative wheat genotypes (carrying dominant Vrn-B1 or Vrn-D1 with recessive vrn-A1) require only 10 to 20 days of chilling; standard to strong winter genotypes (recessive at all three VRN1 homoeologs) require 30 to 60+ days.

vernalization_duration_days.limitations: Represents the standard obligate winter wheat requirement (4 to 8 weeks chilling at 0°C to 7°C per Yan et al. 2003, EV0045). Facultative genotypes requiring only 10 to 20 days of chilling represent a distinct genetic class and are documented in genotype_variation_notes rather than collapsed into a single generalized species value.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Quantitative long-day plant; heading accelerated by photoperiods > 12-14 hours.

growth_stages.description: Elongation of 1.5 cm hollow stem below growing point; mandatory livestock removal point in dual-purpose wheat.
Flowering / anther extrusion; peak vulnerability to heat (>31°C) and Fusarium head blight.

growth_stages.description: Hypocotyl arch emerges and straightens; requires >=18°C soil temperature.
Pyramidal floral bud appears at first fruiting branch (sympodium); 400-500 DD60-F.
First white flower opens; transitions to pink/red within 24-48 hours; 750-850 DD60-F.

growth_stages.stage_name: Peak Bloom / Cutout (Nodes Above White Flower = 5)
growth_stages.description: Peak flowering; terminal vegetative growth slows as bolls demand assimilate; NAWF reaches 5.
Capsules split along suture lines, exposing white lint fibers; 60% open bolls indicates defoliation timing.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Sub-zero temperatures (0°C to -1°C) freeze succulent vegetative tissues and bolls; frost defoliates crop.

absolute_max_survival_c.limitations: Irreversible photosynthetic enzyme denaturation and extreme leaf scorch.

frost_tolerance.description: Extremely sensitive to frost; light frost halts development and causes leaf desiccation.

heat_stress_threshold_c.limitations: Empirical piecewise yield decline breakpoint under field conditions (Schlenker & Roberts 2009 PNAS; 32.0°C); reproductive square/boll shed accelerates above 32-35°C day or >24°C night.

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Temperatures >35°C daytime or night temperatures >24°C inhibit pollen tube elongation and elevate respiration, triggering abscission of small bolls.
Soil temperatures <18.0°C (65°F) cause cold imbibitional chilling injury, root radicle abortion, and severe seedling disease complexes (Rhizoctonia, Pythium).

soil_water_availability_context.description: Requires deep, well-drained loamy sands to silty clay loams; cannot tolerate perched water tables.

irrigation_requirement_context.description: Rainfed in Southeast and Delta; furrow, pivot, or subsurface drip irrigation (250-600 mm net) required in Southern High Plains and Southwest.

seasonal_consumptive_water_use_etc_mm.limitations: Total seasonal consumptive water use (ETc); equates to 24-36 inches (FAO 33; UGA Bull 501).

peak_daily_water_use_mm_day.limitations: Occurs during peak flowering and boll fill (0.28 to 0.40 inches/day).

water_use_efficiency_kg_per_m3.limitations: Measured as kg lint per cubic meter of water (Bordovsky & Mustian 2004).

drought_tolerance.description: Deep taproot provides moderate drought tolerance; sheds fruit under water stress to maintain vegetative survival.

heat_tolerance.description: Vegetative growth adapted to high temperatures; reproductive pollen fertility impaired above 35°C day / 24°C night.

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Extremely sensitive to soil anoxia; root waterlogging >24-48 h triggers ethylene synthesis and catastrophic square and boll shedding.

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Extremely sensitive to soluble subsoil aluminum toxicity below pH 5.5; causes taproot pruning and J-rooting.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: Adapted to calcareous soils in High Plains up to pH 8.2; zinc and iron chlorosis can occur.

salinity_tolerance_ec_e_threshold_ds_m.limitations: Maas & Hoffman (1977) linear response model: saturated soil extract electrical conductivity threshold.

salinity_yield_decline_slope_percent.limitations: Percent yield loss per dS/m increase above 7.7 dS/m threshold: Yr = 100 - 5.2(ECe - 7.7).

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Tolerant per USDA-ARS Maas-Hoffman classification; among the most salt-tolerant major commercial field crops.

soil_texture_preferences.notes: Warms quickly in spring; excellent for early taproot growth in Southeast and Plains.
Premier Mississippi Delta soils; high water-holding capacity.
Optimal aeration and moisture retention.
Prone to waterlogging, crusting, and delayed seedling emergence.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: Critical for taproot aeration and disease suppression.
Requires raised beds and precision drainage.
Causes root anoxia and massive fruit shedding.

effective_water_extraction_depth_cm.limitations: Active root zone containing >=80% of active moisture extraction (3.0 to 4.0 ft per USDA-NRCS NEH 652 Table 3-4).

maximum_anatomical_root_depth_cm.limitations: Maximum vertical penetration of central taproot in uncompacted soils (5.0 to 6.5 ft; Taylor & Klepper 1978).

root_system_architecture.description: Vigorous central taproot with horizontal lateral branches concentrated in the upper 30-60 cm.

compaction_alleviation_potential.description: Taproot is highly vulnerable to right-angle deflection (J-rooting) by hardpans at 15-25 cm depth; requires deep tillage/subsoiling.

nitrogen_uptake_per_unit_yield.limitations: Equates to ~35 lb N per 480 lb lint bale (+ cottonseed) removal (15.9 kg N/bale); total plant uptake is 50-60 lb N/bale.

phosphorus_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: 14 lb P2O5 per 480 lb lint bale (+ cottonseed) removal (6.4 kg P2O5/bale).

potassium_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: 20 lb K2O per 480 lb lint bale (+ cottonseed) removal (9.1 kg K2O/bale). Crop uptake during peak boll fill requires 2-4 lb K2O/ac/day.

has_symbiotic_fixation_capacity.notes: Non-legume malvaceous shrub; lacks symbiotic nitrogen-fixing architecture.

net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha.limitations: Calculation boundary: Partial harvest N removal balance calculated as crop harvest N export in seed cotton (60-110 kg N/ha) minus zero biological N fixation. Does not account for synthetic fertilizer additions (typically 70-120 kg N/ha), soil mineralization, or environmental loss pathways.

nitrogen_balance_assessment.description: Net extractive consumer of soil nitrogen; woody stems decompose slowly without mineralizing significant N.

fertilizer_equivalent_n_credit_lb_ac.limitations: Cotton provides zero fertilizer N credit to subsequent crops.

credit_mechanism.description: Residue is woody and high in lignin; neither immobilizes large N amounts nor releases available N.

release_rate_timing.description: Stalks must be shredded post-harvest; woody root crowns take over a year to decompose.

aboveground_dry_matter_biomass_kg_ha.limitations: Equates to 2.0 to 3.3 dry tons/acre stover.

residue_decomposition_rate.description: Leaves decompose rapidly; stalks are woody and brittle, requiring flail shredding.

ground_cover_rate.description: Provides sparse ground cover post-harvest (<30%); highly vulnerable to winter erosion unless planted to cover crops.

erosion_reduction_potential.description: Poor soil cover leaves fields susceptible to wind erosion in Plains and water erosion in Southeast.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn residue shields emerging cotton seedlings from wind abrasion on sandy Coastal Plain soils.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Requires strict avoidance of atrazine in the corn phase, and intensive Bt monitoring or foliar insecticide management for migrating bollworm.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean provides rotational nitrogen savings (20-30 lb N/ac equivalent) and leaves mellow soil for cotton bedding.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: High reniform nematode risk; verify herbicide carryover and auxin trait compatibility before planting cotton.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Cotton planted into standing or chemically terminated wheat stubble; wheat residue suppresses early-season weeds and protects tender cotton seedlings from blowing sand.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Terminated wheat cover must be killed 2-3 weeks prior to cotton planting to prevent moisture depletion and mitigate thrips migration.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Sorghum residue shields sandy soils from high-velocity wind erosion, protecting emerging cotton seedlings; breaks cotton root-knot and reniform nematodes.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Do not apply residual atrazine on sorghum intended for rotation to cotton the following spring.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn is a non-host to reniform nematode (Rotylenchulus reniformis); rotating cotton with corn suppresses reniform populations and boosts subsequent cotton yields by 10-18% (MSU Pub 2426, EV0096).
compatible_following_crops.limitations: If root-knot nematode is the predominant species, rotating cotton with corn does not provide a biological break.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Alternating broadleaf taproot and fibrous root architecture; soybean fixes nitrogen, improving soil health for cotton.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: In fields infested with reniform nematode, rotating cotton with soybean maintains high nematode pressure without providing a sanitizing break.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Winter wheat seeded into shredded cotton stubble provides critical winter living ground cover, preventing wind and water erosion across the fragile post-harvest cotton landscape.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Late cotton harvest (November/December) can delay wheat planting past optimum window, reducing wheat grain yield potential.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Cotton leaves mellow soil with low residue volume, facilitating early-season sorghum planter penetration; sorghum extracts deep residual moisture.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Low cotton residue increases spring wind erosion vulnerability prior to sorghum canopy closure.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Broadleaf non-host; rootworm larvae starve completely.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Effective biological break for Corn Rootworm (Diabrotica spp.). When corn is rotated with cotton, corn breaks Reniform Nematode (Rotylenchulus reniformis; EV0096); however, corn does NOT break Southern Root-Knot Nematode (Meloidogyne incognita), which reproduces on both corn and cotton.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Broadleaf non-host; breaks soilborne fungal mycelial bridges.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Requires complete volunteer grass control in cotton beds.

shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Rotate with non-host crops (corn or grain sorghum); utilize nematode-resistant cultivars or nematicide seed treatments.
shared_pest_disease_risks.limitations: Both cotton and soybean are excellent reproductive hosts; continuous cotton-soybean rotations compound reniform populations.

shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Plant multi-toxin Bt cotton (Bollgard 3 / WideStrike 3); monitor moth migration from senescing corn.
shared_pest_disease_risks.limitations: High selection pressure for Bt resistance; supplemental diamide insecticides needed during peak flight.

weed_suppression_potential.description: Slow early-season canopy closure and open row architecture leave crop vulnerable to weed competition; requires residual pre-emergence herbicides and layby directed sprays.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: Cotton is sensitive to triazines; requires 12 to 18 month plant-back interval.
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: Severe leaf interveinal chlorosis, stand loss, and stunting if corn atrazine rates exceed labeled limits.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: Ensure cotton trait technology matches applied auxin chemistry (Enlist cotton vs XtendFlex cotton).
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: Sub-lethal off-target drift onto non-traited cotton varieties causes severe epinasty, strapped leaves, and fruit abortion.

continuous_monoculture_penalty.description: 10% to 20% cumulative lint yield reduction in continuous cotton; drives buildup of Verticillium wilt, reniform nematode, and root-knot nematode.

cover_crop_niche.description: Cotton is an indeterminate cash row crop; never managed as a cover crop. (Cereal rye or crimson clover planted after cotton provide winter cover).

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Texas High Plains & Rolling Plains (largest U.S. contiguous acreage). Short thermal season; blowing sand seedling damage; declining irrigation water.
High-yielding alluvial soils; high pest pressure (bollworm, stink bugs); autumn rainfall delaying harvest and degrading lint quality.
San Joaquin Valley & Arizona; 100% irrigated; high water costs and urban competition.
Adapted only in southern Missouri Bootheel; northern Corn Belt lacks necessary DD60 thermal accumulation.

crop_identity.growth_habit: Semi-aquatic erect annual C3 graminoid with lysigenous aerenchyma tissue

active_growth_duration_days.limitations: Range reflects very short-season cultivars (105-115 d in California water-seeded) to full-season Southern long grains (125-140 d in Mid-South drill-seeded).

calendar_occupancy_duration_days.limitations: Field occupancy from initial seeding and flush/flood establishment to pre-harvest drainage and combine harvesting.

growing_degree_days_base_temp_c.limitations: DD50 heat unit system: base temperature is 10.0°C (50°F); upper development threshold is typically 35.0°C (95°F).

growing_degree_days_accumulated.limitations: Equates to 2,100 to 2,800 DD50-F from emergence to 20% grain moisture harvest maturity.

vernalization_required.notes: Subtropical/tropical semi-aquatic grass; zero vernalization requirement for floral induction.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Ancestrally short-day; modern U.S. commercial cultivars have been selected for functional photoperiod insensitivity.

growth_stages.description: Coleoptile penetrates soil surface; requires flushing if topsoil dries.
Primary and secondary tillers form; permanent 5-10 cm flood established immediately following pre-flood N application.
Internode elongation begins; green ring visible above upper node; mid-season N applied.
Panicles emerge from boot; florets open and pollinate within hours; extreme temperature sensitivity.
Panicles turn golden-yellow; grains in lower third firm; fields drained 2-3 weeks prior to harvest.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Sub-zero temperatures (0°C to -1°C) kill vegetative tissues and destroy grain fill.

absolute_max_survival_c.limitations: Enzyme breakdown and total spikelet sterility.

frost_tolerance.description: Extremely sensitive to frost; autumn freezes terminate grain filling.

heat_stress_threshold_c.limitations: Daytime temperatures >35.0°C during flowering cause anther indehiscence and spikelet sterility; nighttime temperatures >24.0°C during grain filling cause severe chalkiness and head rice reduction.

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Night air temperatures <15.0°C (60°F) induce microspore abortion, causing blanking (empty florets). Deep flood water (15-20 cm) acts as a thermal buffer in California checks.
Night temperatures >24.0°C (75°F) accelerate grain respiration, causing incomplete amyloplast packing, white core chalkiness, and reduced head rice milling yield.

seasonal_precipitation_min_mm.limitations: Rice in the U.S. is 100% irrigated; rainfall is a supplemental offset to irrigation pumping.

soil_water_availability_context.description: Requires fine-textured clay or silt loam soils with an impermeable subsoil hardpan to maintain 5-10 cm flood with minimal deep percolation.
soil_water_availability_context.limitations: Silt loam soils require a dense subsoil hardpan (e.g. Crowley silt loam) to impede percolation; self-sealing heavy vertisols (Sharkey clay) maintain flood without mechanical pans; Furrow-Irrigated Rice (row rice) does not require an impermeable hardpan.

irrigation_requirement_context.description: 100% irrigated. Net irrigation requirement ranges from 650 to 1,100 mm (26 to 44 inches) depending on soil percolation and levee management.

seasonal_consumptive_water_use_etc_mm.limitations: Consumptive crop evapotranspiration (ETc); equates to 28-35 inches (FAO 33; Henry et al. 2016). Total field water application is 750-1,500 mm.

peak_daily_water_use_mm_day.limitations: Occurs during heading and early grain fill under high evaporative demand.

water_use_efficiency_kg_per_m3.limitations: Grain yield per unit total water applied (consumptive ETc + field losses).

drought_tolerance.description: Extremely sensitive to soil drying; dropping below saturation during panicle initiation or flowering causes catastrophic spikelet sterility.

heat_tolerance.description: Tolerates high daytime temperatures if humidity is moderate; night heat (>24°C) degrades milling quality.

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Adapted to continuous soil submergence; continuous internal aerenchyma channels transport atmospheric oxygen from leaves down to root tips.
waterlogging_tolerance.limitations: Tolerates continuous root zone submergence (5-15 cm flood) via lysigenous aerenchyma; standard commercial cultivars do not tolerate complete vegetative canopy drowning (>7-10 days submergence).

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Flooding neutralizes acid soils toward pH 6.5-7.0 through microbial reduction of iron and manganese hydroxides.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: Soils with pH >7.3 or high free calcium carbonate induce severe zinc deficiency and seedling chlorosis.

salinity_tolerance_ec_e_threshold_ds_m.limitations: Maas & Hoffman (1977) linear response model: saturated soil extract electrical conductivity threshold.

salinity_yield_decline_slope_percent.limitations: Percent yield loss per dS/m increase above 3.0 dS/m threshold: Yr = 100 - 12(ECe - 3.0).

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Moderately sensitive per USDA-ARS Maas-Hoffman classification; seedling stage is especially sensitive to saline irrigation water (>1.5-2.0 dS/m).

soil_texture_preferences.notes: Sharkey clay and Gumbo soils; very low hydraulic conductivity prevents water loss.
Crowley silt loam / silty clay; premier Arkansas Grand Prairie rice soils.
Suitable if underlain by impermeable traffic hardpan at 15-25 cm.
High percolation rates preclude economical flood maintenance.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: Naturally slow percolation minimizes irrigation pumping costs.
Excellent for contour or zero-grade flood management.
Acceptable only with dense subsoil plow pan.

effective_water_extraction_depth_cm.limitations: Management-oriented root zone (1.0 to 2.0 ft per USDA-NRCS NEH 652 Table 3-4); >90% of active root uptake concentrated in upper 20 cm.

maximum_anatomical_root_depth_cm.limitations: Maximum anatomical root elongation restricted by anaerobic subsoil and dense compaction pan (2.0 to 3.0 ft; Yoshida 1981).

root_system_architecture.description: Superficial adventitious root system with continuous cortical aerenchyma gas lacunae enabling aerobic respiration in submerged soils.

compaction_alleviation_potential.description: Shallow fibrous root system relies on a compacted hardpan to prevent water loss; does not alleviate compaction.

nitrogen_uptake_per_unit_yield.limitations: Equates to 0.60 lb N/bu grain removal (13.3 kg N/t); total plant uptake is 0.90 to 1.10 lb N/bu.

phosphorus_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: 0.30 lb P2O5 per 45 lb bushel grain removal (University of Arkansas MP192).

potassium_removal_per_unit_yield.limitations: 0.18 lb K2O per 45 lb bushel grain removal. Rice straw contains massive potassium (~1.2 lb K2O/bu).

has_symbiotic_fixation_capacity.notes: Non-legume cereal; lacks symbiotic root nodule architecture.

net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha.limitations: Calculation boundary: Partial harvest N removal balance calculated as crop harvest N export in rough rice (90-130 kg N/ha) minus zero biological N fixation. Does not account for synthetic pre-flood fertilizer additions (typically 140-200 kg N/ha), nor massive gaseous loss pathways (denitrification and ammonia volatilization).

nitrogen_balance_assessment.description: Net extractive consumer of soil nitrogen; anaerobic soil conditions require ammonium-N forms (urea); nitrate forms rapidly denitrify.

fertilizer_equivalent_n_credit_lb_ac.limitations: Rice straw provides zero fertilizer N credit to subsequent crops; high silica and C:N immobilize N under aerobic conditions.

credit_mechanism.description: High silica content (10-15%) and C:N (50:1 to 70:1) retard aerobic straw decomposition.

release_rate_timing.description: Slow breakdown under dry conditions; winter flooding significantly accelerates straw decomposition via anaerobic microbial digestion.

aboveground_dry_matter_biomass_kg_ha.limitations: Equates to 3.1 to 4.9 dry tons/acre straw.

residue_decomposition_rate.description: Very slow aerobic decomposition due to 10-15% silica content; winter flooding dramatically accelerates straw breakdown.

ground_cover_rate.description: Heavy straw stubble provides 80-100% surface soil cover post-harvest.

erosion_reduction_potential.description: Flat leveled fields and heavy residue eliminate water and wind erosion.

nitrate_scavenging_efficiency.description: Grown in reduced soil environments with negligible native nitrate.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn breaks rice diseases; heavy corn stubble decomposed under winter flooding.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Strict atrazine prohibition: atrazine residues in anaerobic flooded soil cause severe seedling chlorosis and stand mortality in rice.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Soybean residue mineralizes readily under flood; rice yields follow a 10-15% rotational boost over continuous rice; soybean breaks the red rice seedbank.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Ensure soybean fields are leveled and levee survey lines re-established prior to rice planting.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Rice seeded following wheat harvest or terminated wheat cover crop; wheat utilizes residual moisture and suppresses spring weeds.
compatible_preceding_crops.limitations: Heavy wheat straw residue must be burned or thoroughly incorporated prior to flooding to prevent hydrogen sulfide toxicity and organic acid injury to rice seedlings.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn planted on beds following furrow-irrigated rice (FIR / row rice) or well-drained silt loam ground; breaks rice diseases and exploits deep profile fertility.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Compact subsoil hardpan from flooded rice can restrict corn root penetration unless subsoiled or planted on permanent raised beds.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Premier crop sequence in the Mid-South (1:1 or 2:1 Rice-Soybean); aerobic soybean phase breaks sheath blight fungal sclerotia, allows selective chemical control of weedy red rice with ACCase/ALS herbicides, and restores soil structure.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Heavy clay rice ground must be bedded or surface-drained to prevent soybean waterlogging during summer rains.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Winter wheat drilled into drained, harvested rice ground in early autumn provides winter cash crop and erosion defense in Mid-South.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Late rice harvest or rutted waterlogged clay soils impede seedbed preparation and wheat establishment; requires surface drainage grooves.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Prolonged anaerobic soil submergence drowns rootworm eggs and larvae.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Applicable only to flooded paddy systems; furrow-irrigated rice may permit partial survival.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Prolonged flooding (3-4 months) creates anoxic conditions that substantially reduce viable SCN egg and cyst viability.
pest_disease_break_potential.limitations: Flooding suppresses but does not totally eliminate cysts in levee borders.

shared_pest_disease_risks.target_pest_or_pathogen: Sheath Blight / Aerial Web Blight (Rhizoctonia solani)
shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Rotate with non-host grass crops or plant resistant varieties; apply strobilurin/SDHI fungicides at panicle differentiation.
shared_pest_disease_risks.limitations: Rhizoctonia solani anastomosis group AG1-IA infects both rice (sheath blight) and soybean (aerial web blight).

weed_suppression_potential.description: Continuous 5-10 cm flood water depth exerts extraordinary physical suppression on terrestrial broadleaf and grass weeds.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: Do not rotate corn to flooded rice within 18 months of atrazine application.
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: Atrazine residues in reduced anaerobic flooded soils cause catastrophic seedling chlorosis and stand death in rice.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: Requires 10-month plant-back to drill-seeded rice.
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: Carryover injury appears as leaf necrosis and tillering inhibition in early flush.

continuous_monoculture_penalty.description: 10% to 25% cumulative yield decline in continuous rice monoculture; drives rapid buildup of sheath blight sclerotia, weedy red rice, and straighthead disorder.

cover_crop_niche.description: Rice is a primary grain crop, not managed as a cover crop. (Flooded rice stubble provides premier winter waterfowl foraging habitat).

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Arkansas Grand Prairie, Mississippi River Delta, and Louisiana coastal prairies (>75% of U.S. rice). High nighttime temperatures at grain fill; sheath blight and blast pressure.
Sacramento Valley (medium-grain Calrose). Water-seeded continuous flood; cold night blanking (<15°C); high water and regulatory costs.
Texas Upper Gulf Coast; ratoon (second) cropping practiced; saltwater intrusion in surface canals.
Commercial production restricted to the Missouri Bootheel; northern Corn Belt is thermally unadapted.

crop_identity.growth_habit: Erect cool-season annual C3 small-grain cereal (spring and winter growth habits)

active_growth_duration_days.limitations: Growth habit dependent: Spring barley requires 70-95 active growth days; Winter barley requires 115-150 active growth days (excluding winter dormancy).

calendar_occupancy_duration_days.limitations: Spring barley: 85-110 days (April to July/August); Winter barley: 210-270 days (October to June).

growing_degree_days_base_temp_c.limitations: Standard small-grain thermal base temperature is 0.0°C (32.0°F).

growing_degree_days_accumulated.limitations: Spring barley: 1,100 to 1,500 GDD-C; Winter barley: 1,600 to 2,100 GDD-C to physiological maturity.

vernalization_required.notes: Genotype dependent within single canonical entity: Spring barley requires 0 days vernalization; Winter barley possesses an obligate vernalization requirement of 30 to 50 days between 0°C and 7°C (governed by Vrn-H1/Vrn-H2 allelic variation).
vernalization_required.genotype_variation_notes: Spring cultivars carry dominant Vrn-H1 (represses requirement); winter cultivars carry recessive vrn-H1 alleles requiring cold exposure.

vernalization_duration_days.limitations: 0 days for spring cultivars; 30-50 cumulative days below 7°C for winter cultivars.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Long-day plant; heading accelerates as photoperiod exceeds 14 hours; early heading in spring escapes summer heat.

growth_stages.description: Coleoptile penetrates soil; first leaf emerges; tolerates cold soil (>3-5°C).
Profuse tillering; determines potential spike number per unit area; vernalization occurs in winter types.
First node detectable above soil line; growing point elevates above ground; freeze sensitivity increases.
Spike completely emerged from flag leaf sheath; self-pollination largely complete prior to full emergence.
Kernel pedicel turns brown; dry matter accumulation complete; grain moisture drops to 14-18%.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Spring barley seedlings tolerate -4°C to -6°C; hardened winter barley tolerates crown temperatures down to -12°C to -15°C (less cold-hardy than winter wheat at -20°C).

absolute_max_survival_c.limitations: Rapid leaf desiccation and irreversible grain-fill termination.

frost_tolerance.description: Winter barley has good freezing tolerance (-12°C to -15°C); spring barley tolerates moderate spring frosts (-4°C to -6°C) but is sensitive at heading (-1.5°C).

heat_stress_threshold_c.limitations: Empirical piecewise yield decline breakpoint under field conditions (29-30°C); temperatures >28.0°C during grain filling shorten duration, shrivel kernels, and spike grain protein above malting limits.

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Temperatures >28.0°C impair starch synthase enzymes, reducing starch accumulation and driving grain protein above the 13.5% AMBA malting ceiling.
Freezing temperatures (< -1.5°C) at heading sterilize anthers, causing white head sterility and total floret abortion.

soil_water_availability_context.description: Short growing cycle and cool-season habit make barley highly efficient at extracting stored winter/spring profile moisture.

irrigation_requirement_context.description: Largely dryland in Northern Plains and Pacific Northwest; supplemental irrigation (100-300 mm net) utilized in Intermountain West (ID, MT) for malting barley contracts.

seasonal_consumptive_water_use_etc_mm.limitations: Total seasonal consumptive water use (ETc); equates to 14-22 inches (FAO 33; Bauder EB0161).

peak_daily_water_use_mm_day.limitations: Occurs during boot, heading, and early dough stages.

water_use_efficiency_kg_per_m3.limitations: Highest water productivity among temperate C3 cereals under semiarid dryland conditions.

drought_tolerance.description: High drought tolerance via rapid phenological progression; matures earlier than wheat, escaping late-season terminal drought.

heat_tolerance.description: Sensitive to high temperatures during flowering and grain fill; heat aborts florets and spikes protein.

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Most sensitive of all small grains to soil saturation; root oxygen deprivation for 48 h causes severe chlorosis, tillering abortion, and permanent yield loss.

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Extremely sensitive to soil acidity and soluble aluminum below pH 5.8; severe root pruning occurs below pH 5.5 unless limed.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: Highly adapted to alkaline and calcareous soils up to pH 8.5 in the Northern Plains and Intermountain West.

salinity_tolerance_ec_e_threshold_ds_m.limitations: Maas & Hoffman (1977) linear response model: saturated soil extract electrical conductivity threshold.

salinity_yield_decline_slope_percent.limitations: Percent yield loss per dS/m increase above 8.0 dS/m threshold: Yr = 100 - 5.0(ECe - 8.0).

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Tolerant per USDA-ARS Maas-Hoffman classification; the most salt-tolerant commercial grain crop in global agriculture.

soil_texture_preferences.notes: Optimal water holding and root aeration.
High yield potential in Northern Plains.
Suitable if moisture is adequate; early spring warming.
Prone to waterlogging; poor tillering.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: Essential to prevent root zone anoxia.
Risk of tillering loss and root rot.
Barley fails completely under waterlogged conditions.

effective_water_extraction_depth_cm.limitations: Active moisture extraction depth (2.5 to 4.0 ft per USDA-NRCS NEH 652 Table 3-4).

vernalization_required.notes: Weak facultative flowering response; flowers rapidly under lengthening spring photoperiod without obligate vernalization.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Flowers rapidly under lengthening photoperiod (>12-14 h) in mid-to-late spring.

growth_stages.description: Rapid autumn emergence; develops a prostrate cold-hardy crown rosette with 4-6 true leaves.
Minimal vegetative growth; maintains green rosette under snow or mild winter temperatures.
Explosive erect stem elongation, canopy closure, and rapid biological nitrogen fixation.
Elongated scarlet flower spikes expand; optimal stage for roller-crimper termination and maximum N credit.
Heads turn brown, hard seeds mature, plant naturally senesces.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Air temperatures down to -12°C to -15°C tolerated under insulating snow cover in well-established rosettes (>=4-6 leaves). Bare ground survival is limited to -10°C to -12°C. Susceptible to late-winter freeze-thaw frost-heaving on wet heavy soils.

frost_tolerance.description: Tolerates light autumn frosts; winter-kills in Zone 5 and colder without snow cover.

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Seedling mortality if planted late in autumn without reaching 4 true leaves.
Accelerated senescence, floret blasting, and premature desiccation.

soil_water_availability_context.description: Requires adequate topsoil moisture in September-October for uniform emergence.

irrigation_requirement_context.description: Grown rainfed in the East and South; irrigated in western seed production.

drought_tolerance.description: Shallow root system makes it susceptible to dry spring weather before termination.

heat_tolerance.description: Cool-season annual; senesces rapidly when temperatures exceed 28°C.

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Sensitive to prolonged saturation (>3-5 days); root rot complexes develop rapidly.

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Highly sensitive to aluminum toxicity at pH <5.2; nodulation fails.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: Prone to iron and zinc deficiency chlorosis above pH 7.8.

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Classified as sensitive to soil salinity; yield drops above 1.5 dS/m.

Optimal moisture and nutrient retention.
High yield potential on well-drained sites.
Acceptable if surface drainage prevents ponding.
Prone to standing water and frost-heaving.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: Optimal root development and overwinter survival.
High risk of root rot under heavy spring rains.

root_system_architecture.description: Central taproot with extensive lateral branches concentrated in top 40-60 cm.

compaction_alleviation_potential.description: Cannot penetrate dense subsoil plow pans; improves topsoil tilth.

has_symbiotic_fixation_capacity.notes: Active symbiosis with Rhizobium leguminosarum bv. trifolii (Type R inoculant).

total_gross_n_fixed_kg_ha.limitations: Represents gross biological N fixed in plant biomass at full bloom, not net humified soil organic N accumulation.

effective_fixation_conditions.description: Active nodulation requires pH >5.5, adequate soil phosphorus, and low residual nitrate.

harvested_biomass_nitrogen_export_kg_ha.limitations: Harvest export is 0.0 kg N/ha when managed strictly as green manure cover crop.

net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha.limitations: Calculation boundary: Not applicable as whole-system net soil organic N balance. While unharvested biomass contains 70-150 kg N/ha of fixed biological N, rapid residue decomposition (C:N 12:1-18:1; EV0192) releases mineral N subject to environmental loss pathways (leaching, volatilization, denitrification). Humified soil organic N accumulation is unmeasured. See total_gross_n_fixed_kg_ha for gross biological fixation (70-150 kg N/ha; EV0191) and successor_nitrogen_credit for fertilizer replacement value (40-80 lb N/ac; EV0193).

nitrogen_balance_assessment.description: Supplies substantial biologically fixed nitrogen to the crop rotation.

fertilizer_equivalent_n_credit_lb_ac.limitations: Requires termination at 50-100% bloom. Credit drops to 20-30 lb N/ac if terminated early (vegetative) or on thin stands (<50% cover).

credit_mechanism.description: Rapid decomposition of succulent residue releases mineral N directly into soil solution.

release_rate_timing.description: Over 50% of residue nitrogen is mineralized within 3-5 weeks after spring termination.

residue_decomposition_rate.description: Narrow C:N and low lignin result in rapid decomposition upon spring termination.

ground_cover_rate.description: Reaches 85-98% ground cover by mid-spring, suppressing winter weeds.

erosion_reduction_potential.description: Reduces surface runoff by 40-65% and sediment erosion by 60-80% compared to fallow.

nitrate_scavenging_efficiency.description: Fixes atmospheric N2 rather than scavenging deep subsoil mineral nitrate.

Early soybean harvest leaves clean mellow seedbed for fall clover drilling.
Mid-summer wheat harvest provides ideal August window for clover establishment.
Early summer barley harvest allows timely late-summer clover establishment.
Summer oat harvest provides optimal planting window.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Supplies 40-80 lb N/ac fertilizer credit, zero stover N tie-up, breaks corn rootworm.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Terminate at early-to-full bloom before seed set or excessive spring soil moisture depletion.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Supplies 40-80 lb N/ac replacement credit to sorghum; conserves soil moisture.
Standard conservation tillage rotation; supplies 40-70 lb N/ac to cotton.
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Terminate timely in April to avoid drying coarse sandy soils before cotton planting.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Premier multi-species cover crop mixture or rotation combining N fixation with bio-drilling.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Non-host annual broadleaf legume breaks corn rootworm larval cycle completely.

shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Avoid planting crimson clover in sandy fields with high root-knot nematode pressure preceding cotton.
Rotate with grass crops (corn, wheat, rye) to break Sclerotinia sclerotial buildup.

weed_suppression_potential.description: Rapid early-spring canopy closure smothers winter annual weeds (chickweed, henbit, marestail).

continuous_monoculture_penalty.description: Reseeding crimson clover for multiple consecutive years leads to buildup of Sclerotinia crown rot and root curculio.

cover_crop_niche.description: The standard winter annual legume cover crop for the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Transition Zone.

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Standard winter annual green manure; terminate by mid-April to conserve planting moisture for cotton or corn.
Must be seeded by mid-September for adequate autumn rosette establishment prior to freezing.

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Overwintering is reliable in Zone 6b/7a; winter-kills in Zone 5b without persistent snow cover.

crop_identity.growth_habit: Robust, erect cool-season annual brassica herb with basal rosette of coarse pinnatifid leaves, developing a fleshy cylindrical white storage taproot (15-35 cm length, 2.5-7.0 cm diameter) tapering into a deep vertical penetrating taproot (1.5-2.4 m).

vernalization_required.notes: Non-vernalizing annual habit; long days induce bolting, but late summer plantings remain vegetative until killed by freezing.

photoperiod_sensitivity.description: Long days trigger premature bolting; late-summer seeding prevents flowering.

growth_stages.description: Rapid emergence under warm late-summer soil conditions (within 3-5 days).
Develops broad spreading rosette of coarse leaves; hypocotyl begins fleshy radial swelling.
Massive fleshy root bulking (2-5 cm diameter); vertical taproot drills deep into subsoil (>1.5 m).
100% canopy interception smothers winter annual weeds; aggressively captures 100-200 kg N/ha of soil nitrate.
Sustained sub-freezing temperatures (-7°C) cause intracellular ice crystallization, cellular rupture, and total plant collapse.

absolute_min_survival_c.limitations: Sustained temperatures below -6°C to -9°C (21°F to 15°F) for >=4-6 hours cause 100% cellular rupture and winter-kill in fleshy roots (Weil & Kremen 2007). Survives mild light frosts down to -3°C to -4°C with minor leaf tip burn. Fails to winter-kill in USDA Zones 8b-9 (Deep South/coastal California) where winter temperatures stay above this threshold, requiring chemical burndown or mechanical termination.

frost_tolerance.description: Tolerates light autumn frosts; winter-kills completely under severe sub-zero cold.

critical_thermal_thresholds.physiological_mechanism: Freezing cellular rupture of high-moisture taproot causing complete collapse.
Premature bolting and flower stalk lignification if seeded during summer heat.

soil_water_availability_context.description: Highly responsive to late-summer precipitation for rapid canopy closure.

irrigation_requirement_context.description: Grown almost exclusively rainfed in autumn; irrigated in western arid basins.

drought_tolerance.description: Once established, deep taproots access subsoil moisture; sensitive to seedbed drought at planting.

heat_tolerance.description: Cool-season brassica; high summer heat induces premature bolting.

waterlogging_tolerance.description: Fleshy taproots rot rapidly in ponded or anaerobic saturated soil.

acid_soil_tolerance.description: Tolerates moderate acidity down to pH 5.5 without yield collapse.

alkaline_soil_tolerance.description: Performs well on alkaline and calcareous soils up to pH 8.0.

salinity_tolerance_category.description: Classified as moderately tolerant to soil salinity with threshold around 3.5 dS/m.

soil_texture_preferences.notes: Enables massive taproot elongation and easy root bio-drilling.
Optimal nutrient capture and root fleshing.
High biomass production and profound plow-pan penetration.
Good compaction alleviation if drained.
Prone to waterlogging; restricted root elongation.

soil_drainage_class_preferences.notes: Risk of taproot bacterial soft rot in wet autumns.
Severe taproot rotting and stand death under saturation.

maximum_anatomical_root_depth_cm.limitations: Measured under unconstrained or macropore-rich deep loess and coastal plain soils (Weaver 1926; Chen & Weil 2010); effective moisture extraction remains concentrated in upper 60-120 cm; subsoil penetration is severely reduced in saturated or severely compacted (>3.5 MPa) subsoils.

root_system_architecture.description: Swollen white daikon storage taproot (15-35 cm) tapering into vertical penetrating fine taproot (1.5-2.4 m).

compaction_alleviation_potential.description: Punches through dense subsoil plow pans (>2.0 MPa); leaves open 2-5 cm macropores upon winter decay.
compaction_alleviation_potential.limitations: Measured in Maryland coastal plain silt loam and sandy loam soils with traffic pans (Chen & Weil 2010); bio-drilling efficacy is conditional on early autumn establishment (>=6-8 weeks prior to freeze) and fails in waterlogged, smeared, or severely rutted soils.

has_symbiotic_fixation_capacity.notes: Non-legume; lacks symbiotic nitrogen-fixing nodule architecture.

effective_fixation_conditions.description: Non-legume; scavenges soil mineral nitrogen instead of fixing atmospheric N2.

harvested_biomass_nitrogen_export_kg_ha.limitations: Harvest export is 0.0 kg N/ha in unharvested cover crop mode (100% biomass returned to soil).

net_soil_nitrogen_balance_kg_ha.limitations: Calculation boundary: Set to null because 0.0 kg N/ha derived solely from zero biological fixation minus zero harvest export does not represent a measured whole-system net soil nitrogen balance. Oilseed radish is a non-fixing brassica (0.0 kg N/ha BNF; EV0199) that recycles 100-220 kg N/ha of scavenged profile nitrate (EV0206) rather than introducing newly fixed atmospheric N. Whole-system net soil organic N change is unmeasured. Rapid spring mineralization (70-80% in March-April; EV0207, EV0208) releases mineral N subject to early-spring leaching on coarse soils before cash crop uptake.

nitrogen_balance_assessment.description: Exceptional nitrate scavenger; recycles mineral N but provides 0.0 kg/ha net biological addition.

fertilizer_equivalent_n_credit_lb_ac.limitations: Oilseed radish does not provide an additive biological nitrogen fertilizer credit (0.0 lb N/ac biological addition). However, recycling and rapid mineralization of 100-200 lb N/ac of scavenged profile nitrogen provides an effective rotational N benefit of 20-40 lb N/ac on subsequent corn if captured by crop roots before leaching.

credit_mechanism.description: Rapid early spring mineralization releases captured nitrate into upper soil profile.

release_rate_timing.description: Over 70-80% of captured N is mineralized in March-April upon winter-kill thaw.

residue_decomposition_rate.description: Succulent low-lignin tissues decompose completely over winter upon freezing.

ground_cover_rate.description: Reaches near-100% canopy cover within 3-4 weeks, smothering winter weeds.

erosion_reduction_potential.description: Excellent autumn erosion control; leaves bare soil by late spring after total residue breakdown.

nitrate_scavenging_efficiency.description: Captures 100-220 kg N/ha of residual nitrate from upper 1.5 m of soil profile.

compatible_preceding_crops.synergy_mechanisms: July wheat harvest provides ideal full 60-80 day window for massive radish taproot growth.
August wheat harvest precedes fall radish catch cropping in Northern Plains.
Early summer barley harvest allows 8-10 week window for bio-drilling.
Mid-summer oat harvest provides optimal August planting window.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Corn roots utilize open radish biopores to bypass dense plow pans to access subsoil water; field studies in Maryland and Michigan observed a 5-10% corn yield increase on compacted no-till soils (Chen & Weil 2011; MSU E-3165).
compatible_following_crops.limitations: Corn yield benefit is conditional on soil compaction and late-summer water stress; no yield increase is observed on uncompacted soils or in well-watered seasons. On coarse sands, early nitrate release can leach before late-spring corn uptake unless companion rye is used.

compatible_following_crops.synergy_mechanisms: Winter-killed radish leaves clean, weed-free, warm seedbed for no-till soybean.
Allows ultra-early no-till spring wheat seeding into warm, mellow soil.
Winter-killed radish seedbed provides ideal firm, mellow seedbed for spring alfalfa.

pest_disease_break_potential.break_mechanism: Non-host brassica interrupts SCN reproduction cycle; juveniles fail to establish feeding sites (Melakeberhan et al. 2010). Note: Does not actively trap SCN cysts (unlike specialized European beet cyst nematode trap radishes).
Non-host broadleaf cover crop provides complete biological break.

shared_pest_disease_risks.risk_mitigation: Exercise caution and extend rotation intervals (3-4 years) when rotating with commercial brassica cash crops (canola, cabbage, broccoli) in fields with Clubroot history; maintain soil pH >6.8-7.2 to suppress spore germination.
shared_pest_disease_risks.limitations: Plasmodiophora brassicae resting spores survive for >10 years in acidic soils (pH <6.8). Represents an agronomic disease management risk, not a statutory prohibition.

weed_suppression_potential.description: Rapid canopy closure smothers chickweed, henbit, and winter annual broadleaf weeds.

herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.label_specific_restriction: moderate_to_high
herbicide_carryover_sensitivities.limitations: Atrazine residues cause severe stunting and chlorosis in establishing brassica seedlings.

continuous_monoculture_penalty.description: Continuous brassica monoculture builds up soil-borne Clubroot and flea beetle populations.

cover_crop_niche.description: The benchmark cover crop for soil compaction alleviation and autumn nitrate scavenging.

regional_suitability.regional_limitations: Requires planting by early September for full taproot development; winter-kills completely in December.
Planted following small grain harvest; winter-kills in late October/November, allowing early spring wheat seeding.
Premier bio-drilling cover crop; winter-kills reliably in January across most of the basin.

evidence_registry.variety_scope: Hexaploid bread wheat (2n=6x=42, AABBDD genome, spring habit)
